speaker_role: current admissions officer (Harvard), shared as a clip on the ElevatEd School channel
commercial_incentive: hosted on a consulting company's (ElevatEd School) channel, though this specific clip is a reused Harvard-sourced statement rather than a direct pitch
key_insights: States that Harvard applications are complete without standardized test scores and are reviewed in full by a human admissions officer either way.
States that admissions officers at Harvard read hundreds of test-optional applications weekly and admit many test-optional candidates.
Says whether omitting scores hurts an application is genuinely mixed ('somewhere between not really and it depends'), not a simple yes or no.
Says international applicants generally have more leeway to go test-optional, since test access/scheduling can be much harder in some regions.

Says students from well-resourced schools (especially top public/private schools with a track record of Ivy admits) who opt out while peers at their school submit scores may look suspicious to readers.
Concludes the right choice on submitting scores depends on the individual student's school profile and geography, not a universal rule.
specific_numbers_or_facts: Harvard admissions officer states colleagues read 'hundreds' of test-optional applications every week.
notable_or_distinctive: Direct on-record statement attributed to a sitting Harvard admissions officer nuancing test-optional strategy by school context and geography, rather than treating it as a blanket policy.
reliability_notes: Very short clip (261 words); presented as a direct quote from a named institution's admissions officer, which lends it more credibility than most clips in this batch, though the original interview context/date is not given and it is reposted on a third-party consulting channel.
